note: Rewritten to the claim that survived the four independent audits.

problems.original_statement: A deterministic treatment strategy can assign a treatment that clinicians almost never give to patients with certain covariate histories. The standard response is to inspect the weight distribution and truncate the tail, which reduces variance, changes the implicit estimand and can leave substantial bias in place. What the diagnostic does not report is the quantity a reader needs: what fraction of the target population has no support for the strategy under study, which histories are the unsupported ones, and what estimand remains identified once they are set aside. A 2026 study of non-mutually exclusive assignment found that poor overlap defeated adjustment methods that were otherwise well specified, which is the failure mode a weight histogram is least able to show.
problems.correction_note: Truncation is bias-variance regularization and does not change the estimand in the way the entry implied; what it cannot do is identify an effect under structural nonpositivity. Software for stochastic and modified treatment policies also partly addresses the continuous longitudinal case, so the alternatives the entry proposes are not entirely unavailable.
problems.statement: A deterministic treatment strategy can assign a treatment that clinicians almost never give to patients with certain covariate histories. The standard response is to inspect the weight distribution and truncate the tail. Truncation is bias-variance regularization: it cannot identify an effect where the treatment density is structurally zero, and a marginal weight summary does not say which intervention-relevant histories carry small or zero density. What a reader needs and does not get is a policy-specific support criterion fixed in advance, diagnostics localized by time and by history, the fraction of the target population that fails the criterion, and the estimand that survives once those strata are set aside. Empirically, poor overlap has been shown to defeat adjustment methods that were otherwise well specified, which is the failure a weight histogram is least able to show. Software for stochastic and modified treatment policies covers part of the continuous longitudinal case; partial-identification bounds for arbitrary sustained strategies do not exist.
problems.why_open: Practical positivity is a property of a conditional density over a growing history, so beyond a few time points the object to be diagnosed is high-dimensional and cannot be plotted. Truncation is attractive precisely because it converts an identification failure into a variance reduction, which reads as a modeling improvement rather than as a change of question. Reporting an unsupported fraction also requires deciding what counts as support, and any such criterion is a decision about the estimand that nobody is currently required to state.
problems.proposed_direction: Prespecify a policy-specific support criterion, report time- and history-localized support diagnostics against it, and report the sensitivity of the conclusion to the criterion, so the definition is visible rather than implicit. Replace or restrict deterministic regimes the data cannot support with modified treatment policies, incremental propensity-score interventions or stochastic initiation rules where that is scientifically acceptable, and say so in the paper rather than in the truncation. Derive partial-identification bounds for the unsupported strata under sustained strategies, which is the piece no current software supplies.
